title: Toscana Is Italy's Thermometer: Regional Petrol Lands Exactly on the National Average
dek: On August 6th self-service Benzina in Toscana priced at €2.0065 — the national self-service average to the fourth decimal — while diesel eased for a third straight day.
body: Self-service drivers in Toscana paid €2.0065 for Benzina and €2.1205 for Gasolio on August 6th. The petrol figure is the striking one: it matches the national self-service average of €2.0065 to the fourth decimal place, an exact tie rather than a rounding coincidence. Diesel sits just 0.06 cents above the national €2.1199. The region only separates itself at the pump attendant's window — full-service Benzina runs €2.1794 against €2.1459 nationally, a gap of more than three and a third cents that reflects a network leaning on August tourist and motorway traffic.

The direction of travel is gently downward. Self-service Benzina has now slipped for a third consecutive day, down 0.39 cents from its August 4th peak of €2.0104, while Gasolio has given back 0.63 cents over the same span, from €2.1268 to €2.1205. Metano is the outlier, jumping 1.67 cents in a single day to €1.6140 and now standing nearly six cents above the national figure of €1.5537. The reporting network behind these numbers held firm: 1,648 stations registered across Toscana, 1,490 of them filing prices — a 90.4% reporting rate, effectively level with the 90.7% recorded nationally (21,738 of 23,961).

Resolving a market down to this level — one region a day, four fuels, self and full service, with the running history behind each one — is not something a hand-maintained spreadsheet survives for long. Fuel Dashboard rebuilds itself every morning instead: it pulls the MIMIT open data, aggregates it by region, regenerates the charts and republishes the site without anyone opening a file. The whole pipeline was built with Claude Code, and the payoff is that the effort moves off maintaining the data and onto reading it.
pull_quote: Toscana's self-service petrol came in at €2.0065 — identical to the national average down to the fourth decimal.
caption:
Today's Fuel Dashboard spotlight is Toscana, and it produced an unusually clean number: self-service Benzina at €2.0065, which is exactly the national self-service average, matching to the fourth decimal place. Diesel is barely distinguishable too, €2.1205 regionally against €2.1199 nationally.

Underneath that stillness there is movement. Self-service petrol in Toscana has fallen for three days running, down 0.39 cents from its August 4th peak, with diesel off 0.63 cents over the same stretch. Metano went the other way entirely: up 1.67 cents in twenty-four hours to €1.6140, now almost six cents above the national average. And the region does break away on full service, €2.1794 versus €2.1459 nationally. Of 1,648 registered stations in Toscana, 1,490 reported prices today.

These figures come from Fuel Dashboard, a project that tracks Italian fuel prices daily from MIMIT open data — national and regional averages across Benzina, Gasolio, GPL and Metano, self and full service, with day-by-day history and a different region in the spotlight every morning. You can browse it here: https://adeo-blip.github.io/fuel-price-italy/

The more interesting part is not the data, it's the method. A dashboard like this maintained by hand in Excel dies within two weeks: download the CSV, clean it, recompute, re-export the charts, repeat forever. Instead the whole pipeline runs itself every morning — ingest, aggregate, regenerate, republish — and I built all of it with Claude Code. That is the real argument for AI coding tools: not writing code faster, but making projects sustainable that otherwise would not be worth starting.
